newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Euro needs one voice internationally - Commission.
newsitem.headline: Euro needs one voice internationally - Commission.

text.p: An unresolved and important issue for Europe's planned single currency is just who will represent member countries in international policy discussions, the European Commission said on Wednesday.
In assessing the external dimension of economic and monetary union (EMU), the EU executive failed to reach any firm judgments on who would speak for the euro.

"The direct implication of EMU is that the EU will have a single exchange rate and a single monetary policy, and that it will be the policy mix at the European level that is relevant for the rest of the world," the Commission's report said.
Noting that it was clear the EU had to establish a common position on matters that required international coordination, EU commissioner Yves Thibault de Silguy said no solution had yet been found.
"We will have to see how we will organise representation at the international level," EU commissioner Yves Thibault de Silguy told a news conference.
"We need to have a single expression of Europe's positions. It is a real problem." he added.

The Commission's working document underlined that primary responsibility for external policy matters rested with EU finance ministers but that both the Commission and a future European Central Bank had roles to play.
In addition, the EU executive said the decision on who would represent euro members would require unanimity.
